title: First Suspect Detained in Ojocaliente Car Bomb, Caught With Grenade and Homemade Explosive in Cuauhtémoc, Zacatecas
detail: On September 1, 2026, Zacatecas security forces detained the first suspect linked to the August 30 Ojocaliente car bomb attack: Juan Pedro 'N,' 29, from Aguascalientes, captured during an operation in Cuauhtémoc municipality, Zacatecas. Officers spotted him driving a Nissan; he threw spike strips (ponchallantas) onto the road, abandoned the vehicle, and tried to flee into farmland before being caught. Seized from him: a homemade 'niple'-type explosive device, a fragmentation grenade, 22 spike-strip devices, five loaded magazines, and quantities of substances consistent with marijuana, methamphetamine, and cocaine. Zacatecas Security Secretary Arturo Medina Mayoral said 'hay información suficiente para decir que formó parte del equipo que llevó a cabo el atentado' (there is sufficient information to say he was part of the team that carried out the attack), though judicial determination of his role remained pending. The Nissan he was driving was separate from the Seat used in the August 30 bombing itself, which had been reported stolen in Jalisco in April 2026. Authorities said operations continued to locate additional suspects.

media.caption: First suspect detained in connection with the Ojocaliente, Zacatecas car bomb attack

confidenceReason: The arrest, seized items, and circumstances are independently reported by two Tier-2 outlets; the suspect's specific role in the car bomb attack rests on the state security secretary's preliminary assessment, with judicial confirmation still pending.

title: Colima SSPC and Navy Detain Two Suspected CJNG/Los Mezcales Members in Manzanillo, Seize 40mm Grenade Launcher
detail: On September 1, 2026, elements of the Colima State Security and Citizen Protection Secretariat (SSPC) and the Mexican Navy (SEMAR) detained Bernardo Alexander 'N' and José Roberto 'N' in the port city of Manzanillo, Colima, identifying them via intelligence reports as suspected violence generators tied to CJNG and its Colima-based armed wing 'Los Mezcales.' Authorities seized a .380-caliber handgun with a loaded magazine and cartridges, a 40-millimeter grenade launcher, and bags of a granulated substance consistent with methamphetamine. The detainees and evidence were turned over to the Federal Attorney General's Office (FGR) in Manzanillo. The state's Mesa de Coordinación Estatal para la Construcción de Paz y Seguridad said the operation followed a separate, earlier Colima capital arrest of Kevin Felipe 'N,' Luis Daniel 'N,' and a minor, also linked to Los Mezcales.
